title: Tell cell authors and workers that the contract guards exist
action:
The five code cells of this feature shipped two guards that refuse work at the claim and dispatch doors, and one prompt change every worker now sees. Nobody has been TOLD. A guard nobody was told about is a trap. This cell is prose only - no code, no tests, no behaviour change - and it closes the three doc doors bee close names.

Step 1 - the worker-facing rule, in skills/bee-swarming/SKILL.md. Read the shipped behaviour first in docs/knowledge/areas/workflow-state/dispatch.md, which cells scor-4 and scor-5 already synced; do not invent from this cell's prose. Add to the worker contract, in the skill's own compressed voice and in as few lines as it takes: a claim or dispatch is REFUSED when the cell cites a decision that is retired or whose trigger is waiting or due (codes CONTRACT_RETIRED and CONTRACT_UNSETTLED), and a test-writing cell that cites no contract-tagged decision is refused by the mint trap. Both refusals are typed and zero-mutation and name their own remedy. Say plainly that an entry in cell.decisions which does not resolve to a store decision - a local D-ID like D1 - is passed over, never refused. Also add one line that the worker prompt now carries the user's verbatim request under a DO-NOT-PARAPHRASE header, and that no layer may replace or paraphrase it.

Step 2 - the author-facing rule, in skills/bee-planning/SKILL.md, in the cell quality rules. One rule: a cell that writes tests against an interface cites that interface's contract decision by its store id in cell.decisions, because the mint trap refuses a test-writing cell that cites none. Name the honest limit in the same breath - the trap sees a test-shaped path in files or role test, so a code-role cell adding an inline test module to a source file is NOT caught, and citing is on the author. Keep it to the rule, not the mechanism; point at the area spec.

Step 3 - the routing door. bee close reports 6 unrouted locked D-IDs for this feature. Each of D1 to D6 must be cited, in the form "slp-contract-original-request D<n>" (plain, a range, or a slash-list), inside a docs/knowledge/ bundle file. Place each citation where the rule it produced actually lives: D1 and D2 in the decision-memory overview beside the derived contract status and the namespaced tag; D3 and D4 in workflow-state dispatch.md beside the tripwire and the mint trap; D5 and D6 in hook-runtime the-intent-anchor-and-compaction-survival.md beside the dispatch reach. Do not move or restate the rules those files already carry - add the citation to the line that already states the rule. Re-run bee close --feature slp-contract-original-request --dry-run and confirm the routing door reads clear before you cap.

Step 4 - the doc-deferral door, which bee close reports for nine lines. Two different cases, and they take different answers.
(a) docs/product-description/memory/decisions.md lines 17, 62, 63, 68, 114, 117 and 161 do not promise future work: they DOCUMENT bee's own deferral machinery, quoting the very vocabulary the guard scans for (defer, for now, revisit when, later). That is the case the door's own remedy names. Wrap each in a reasoned block - <!-- bee:not-a-deferral: <reason> --> ... <!-- /bee:not-a-deferral --> - with a reason saying it describes the deferral guard rather than deferring anything. Group adjacent lines under one block where they are adjacent; do not change a word of the prose itself.
(b) docs/history/slp-contract-original-request/CONTEXT.md's four "Deferred To Planning" checkboxes were all ANSWERED by planning, and the answers are in plan.md. Tick each box and append the one-line answer with a pointer to the plan section that carries it: the test-writing signal (plan.md, Approach S5), the tripwire's door (Approach S4 - both doors), the anchor resolution (Approach Half B - feature-keyed, no default fallback), and the byte-identical render (Risk map, proven by no_resolvable_anchor_leaves_every_runtime_and_kind_pair_byte_identical). Do NOT touch the Locked Decisions table, the terms, or any other section - those are the historical record. The "Deferred Ideas" entry names a scope-out D1 already made, so no condition could ever fire for it: wrap it in the same reasoned not-a-deferral block.

Step 5 - skills/ is a release-manifest root, so a skill edit and a rebuilt manifest are one unit of work. Run bee dev regen (render-skill-trees, then onboard --repo-root . --apply, then release-manifest --write, in that order) and commit the regenerated manifest and skill trees with the rest.

Step 6 - before capping, run bee close --feature slp-contract-original-request --dry-run one more time and report in your outcome which doors now read clear and which remain. The scribing-debt, judge-debt and uat doors are the orchestrator's, not yours - do not act on them.
